summary: Dual-control approval for timeboxed VPC inference log rehydration for customer data remediation
description:
Issue summary: Customer support escalated a request to rehydrate a small set of inference sessions from a VPC-bound private deployment to correct PII in a customer record. Impact: One enterprise customer (internal account id 0442) has requested remediation of four sessions suspected to contain unredacted personal data. Access must be timeboxed and dual-control approved before any decryption/rehydration.

Request details: Support/CS asks SRE/Platform to restore the following artifacts from S3 archival storage in the customer VPC workspace, unwind encryption for the minimal session slices, and produce a sanitized export for legal/customer remediation. Artifacts list: session-logs (sharded), KV-cache snapshots, and request/response payloads for session IDs: s-20260214-001, s-20260217-047, s-20260218-003, s-20260220-011.

Approval requirements: Per prod log access runbook, we require two approvers from the following groups: Security (Privileged Access), Compliance, and Platform SRE. Access must be mediated by a short-lived role with KMS key-use restrictions and split-approval recorded in the audit log. Export must be redacted by an approved pattern before leaving the VPC.

Access controls & plan: 1) Create ephemeral role ephemeral-access-INT-128334 with minimum privileges. 2) Restore relevant object slices to a restricted scratch bucket within the same VPC. 3) Use KMS rewrap to allow ephemeral decrypt; all KMS operations logged. 4) Run sanitization script per Confluence redaction patterns (confluence link provided). 5) Produce redaction-report and return sanitized bundle to Customer Success. 6) After handoff, destroy scratch bucket and revoke role; record actions in audit.

Data minimization: We will only rehydrate the four session IDs. No global table scans or broad exports. The sanitized bundle will include only timestamps, routing metadata, and redacted user text per pattern; raw PII fields will be hashed or removed.

Retention & audit: All steps recorded; decrypted artifacts destroyed after verification. KMS audit and S3 server access logs will be attached to ticket.

Risks & mitigations: Potential for accidental over-exposure if redaction rules miss variants. Mitigation: pair-review of redaction output by Security and Compliance before handing to CS. Also use read-only copies and prevent copy-out until approved.

Next steps requested: 1) Security lead to approve dual-control by 2026-03-12 EOD. 2) Platform SRE to schedule ephemeral role and restore window (target 2026-03-13). 3) Compliance to sign off on redaction pattern. 4) CS to prepare customer communication template.
